links_touching_record.rationale: The contactor design record's interfaces field is a signal table naming the command and feedback signals. FB2-SW-IFS-000003 replaces it with the four declared elements, the two precondition assertions on every actuation request, the two-value return contract and the finding that the negative value is ambiguous between a registry miss and a completed request. It refines FB2-SW-DSN-000003 and sits alongside FB2-SW-DSN-000006, whose detailed design names the registry data model and the four-way feedback dispatch and still states no interface contract.

FB2-SW-SIR-000002 is the software interface requirement set for the actuation boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000003 (contactor actuation and feedback driver). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.

not_specified_by_source: The interface returns STD_OK when the request has been placed on a registry entry, not when the contactor has closed. Nothing here reports the resulting electrical state; that is what CONT_GetContactorState and CONT_CheckFeedback are for, and neither is named by this element.

The interface does not state that the request is forwarded to the SPS module by name or what happens if that forward fails. The forward is SPS_RequestContactorState(..., SPS_CHANNEL_ON) at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L195 and its return value is not read, so a failure inside the SPS module is invisible here.

The interface does not state BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, the size of the registry it searches. That is (2u * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) + BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L237.

The interface does not state whether a request for a contactor that is already closed is idempotent, accepted or rejected. The implementation sets the same field and returns STD_OK, so it is idempotent in effect, but that is not stated.

not_specified_by_source: The interface reports a mismatch as a diagnosis event and nothing else, so a caller cannot distinguish 'contactor open when it should be closed' from 'contactor closed when it should be open'. The diagnosis id and the string index are passed, and the polarity is lost at this boundary.

The interface does not state how many contactors it checks. The body iterates BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS, defined as (2u * BS_NR_OF_STRINGS) + BS_NR_OF_CONTACTORS_OUTSIDE_STRINGS at src/app/application/config/battery_system_cfg.h L237.

The source carries an open item in the interface itself: a TODO in the body at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L130 saying that a check that only one contactor of each type is configured for each string is still to be added. The interface therefore does not guarantee that a string has exactly one contactor per type, and this record does not claim it does.
The interface does not state a debounce or a settling time, so it does not say whether a transient mismatch during switching is expected to be reported.

interface_level_gaps.consequence: No single element of this interface lets a caller close a contactor and learn that it closed. A requirement about actuation has to be written across two elements, and the source does not state the pair as a contract.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: STD_OK is set at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L196 immediately after the SPS forward at L195, with no confirmation of the resulting state.
interface_level_gaps.gap: The interface never reports the electrical outcome of a request. Closing returns STD_OK when the request is placed on a registry entry, and the electrical state is a separate read through CONT_GetContactorState.

interface_level_gaps.consequence: A caller cannot distinguish a configuration error, which no amount of retrying will fix, from a transient condition. A requirement that says the interface shall report failure distinctly per cause is not satisfiable against this implementation.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The initial STD_NOT_OK at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L187 is returned unchanged both when the loop finds no matching registry entry, at L200, and on the path where the forward to the SPS module has already been made.
interface_level_gaps.gap: STD_NOT_OK is ambiguous between two different situations.

interface_level_gaps.consequence: A failure reported by the SPS module does not reach the caller of the contactor interface, so the interface cannot signal it.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: SPS_RequestContactorState is called at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L195 and its return value is not assigned or tested on the following lines.
interface_level_gaps.gap: The forward to the actuator is unchecked.

interface_level_gaps.consequence: The interface does not guarantee one contactor per type per string, so a caller reading a contactor state may be reading an arbitrary one of several.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The TODO at src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c L130 states that the check that only one contactor of each type is configured for each string is still to be added.
interface_level_gaps.gap: The feedback interface carries an open item in the source itself.

providing_module.name: Contactor driver
providing_module.role: Acts on the contactors and reads their feedback. It keeps the commanded state and the feedback separately and forwards actuation requests to the SPS module.

revision_history.description: Four elements of the contactor driver: the close request, the state read, the feedback check and the unconditional open sweep. Two findings are recorded from the source rather than smoothed over: STD_NOT_OK is ambiguous between a refused request and a registry miss, and the feedback check carries an open TODO about contactor-type uniqueness per string.

verification_status.statement: The contract above was read from the source at the pinned commit and has not been compared with what the code does when it runs. Every behavioural statement is a reading of the implementation text, not an observation of behaviour. Where the two could differ, this record does not know.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SW-IFS-000003` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
